newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds drag Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Golds drag Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: The Australian stock market closed lower on Tuesday as sliding metal prices pushed the resources sector lower, just offsetting industrial stocks which gained ground on continued support for the banking sector.
The All Ordinaries index fell 4.9 points to 2285.5.
The gold sector led miners down. The gold index fell over three percent after the gold price failed to rebound in Asian markets after passing through US$380 in New York on Monday.
After being quoted at US$378.15/378.65 at New York's close, gold at 0610 GMT was quoted at US$377.90/378.40 in Hong Kong.
"Gold has been the standout, (the gold index) losing over three percent," said broker Justin Hondris of brokerage Hartley Poynton.
"Technically, chartists are saying US$380 was the level and it's gone through that. There are a few nerves about where it goes from here," he said.

Highlighting the focus on gold, base metals miners CRA and BHP rebounded strongly off their day's lows to finish at or near square while WMC, with a greater exposure to gold, only just dragged itself off the floor by the close.
BHP closed five cents lower at A$16.15 and CRA shares was unchanged at A$19.00 while WMC closed 21 cents lower at A$7.92.

Industrial stocks were bolstered by another strong performance from the banks which continued to rise as traders speculated that another interest rate cut could occur as soon as Wednesday. The Reserve Bank board met on Tuesday and its monetary policy announcements are typically made the next day.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
